chapter: Central Avenue, WPA and the Alabam era
title: The Central Avenue scene of the late thirties and forties
summary: Redd asks about the real Central Avenue; they name Marie Dickerson, Nat King Cole, Alton Redd, the Royal brothers, C.P. Johnson and the Club Alabam players.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Mr. Blakeney, as you probably know--I'm sure you know, having been one of the pioneers of the Central Avenue era, there has been much, much misinformation about Central Avenue during the late thirties into the forties and fifties. Kindly brief us on the real Central Avenue, the real Central Avenue scene.
Let us know about when the black musicians started to ignite the area with their vibrant bands and shows, and who were some of these black musicians that were very active during this time.
What time would this be now?
This would be the late thirties into the forties. Central Avenue was hot.
Late thirties into the forties--that's when the Alabam was popular. There was a piano player back in those days, Marie Dickerson.
Marie Dickerson was also I think the first licensed black woman aviatrix in the State of California.
Yes, I think so.
And her name is now Marie Coker, she was married to the late trombonist Henry Coker.
That's right.
She was an entertainer; is that right?
That's right.
Who were some of the other instrumentalists? Was Nat King Cole on the scene then?
I guess he was, yes. So was Alton, so was your dad back in those days.
Alton Redd. What about the Royal Brothers?
Back in those days they were pretty popular too, they were coming up.
Was that Marshall and Ernie?
That's right. I didn't watch Ernie too much.
He came on later. Do you remember C.P. Johnson?
Oh yes, I remember
C.P.
Can you remember some of the members of his band? He played at the Club Alabam.
That's right. No, I can't recall any of the members of his band.
Kirk Bradford--do you remember Kirk Bradford?
Kirk Bradford played alto sax.
That's right.
Buddy Collette perhaps in the early forties, he was a member of the C.P. Johnson orchestra. Johnson was a bongo player, very flamboyant.
Yes.
T-Bone Walker,was he in there? Did he come in and out of the Club Alabam?
I don't remember.
You don't remember
Not too well. Back in those days I might remember him.
Did T-Bone Walker come on in the forties perhaps, more closer to World War II?
I'm trying to remember when did he come on.
